description.purpose: The trigger for an export, from the OS side: it turns `{target: <member path>}` into a message on the lane the memory that has to answer accepts, and renders what comes back into one sentence.
description.use_when: Reached only through this hive's `in_dump` door. The export itself is written where the memory stands; what happens here is the ASKING.
description.not_in_scope: No dump, no format, no file and no store. It owns no part of what an export produces -- a cell that assembled one here would have made the colony operator's decision about where the record lives.
description.emits_meaning: route export: the request, carrying `hop.target` -- the path of the member whose memory is to be exported -- and, when the caller named one, `hop.export_to`, the directory of this run relative to the fence each holder's store declares (GH #555). The level below re-stamps it onto `in_export` and relays it unchanged; nothing here knows the shape of the memory it is addressing. route receipt: what the export answered, or the refusal that it named no target.
description.consumes_meaning: The request as a tool_call turn: `{target, export_to?, since?}`. `hop.target` is read as a fallback, so an edge may address a member without a body.
examples: in_dump {target: '/os/orgs/acme/members/alex'} -> export, hop.target set, one message down
in_dump with no target -> receipt, hop.error_code 'export_target_missing' -- an export with no address is a request every memory could believe was meant for it
export_done with hop.error_code -> receipt naming the code
in_dump {target: '/os/orgs/acme/members/alex', export_to: 'nightly-2026-09-04'} -> export, hop.export_to set; each holder writes <fence>/nightly-2026-09-04/<hive>/seed/
